content.text: The text combines several works. In Mugsborough, poverty-stricken workers are manipulated into supporting rival Liberal and Tory candidates; Socialist organizers face violence, while Ruth leaves Easton, later reconciles with him, and gives her baby to the Owens. Owen confronts Rushton over Bert White’s freezing workplace. Barrington aids poor children and supports Socialism. The narrative ends with capitalist hypocrisy contrasted with hopes for a cooperative future. A separate adventure follows Heywood and Rudolph through tunnels and a besieged Chinese nunnery; they escape by Hakka boat, while Heywood returns after being presumed dead. Scientific articles discuss lime kilns, apple jelly, grape bags, solar heat, meridian-finding, pheasants, trees, and American woods. Other excerpts describe children’s bodily organs, nutrition, alcohol, tobacco, circulation, breathing, skin, senses, and warmth. A biography and interview portray Boer president Paul Kruger in Pretoria, defending Transvaal independence and opposing England, followed by an account of Cecil Rhodes’s rise through diamond mining and imperial ambition.
